rendered: The premise is not supported: the paper does not use copper current collectors. The anode-free cell is built on carbon/Al electrodes, and the authors explain that they chose aluminum over copper.[1] The stated reason is cost and weight. Copper was ruled out because Al offers a cost benefit of ∼3× cheaper[2] and a weight benefit of ∼3× lighter[3], which the authors call a great advantage made available by transitioning to sodium-based chemistries. Copper appears in the paper only as a point of comparison: prior work using Cu electrodes reported nearly double the hysteresis at higher current, so the authors' own cell is not copper-based.[4]
